title: Women Vote in First Chilean Presidential Election
note: Confirmed: first presidential election with women's suffrage; Ibanez won with 46.8%. Women gained suffrage in 1949, first exercised in presidential election 1952.

title: Central Unica de Trabajadores (CUT) Founded
note: Founded February 12, 1953 under Clotario Blest. Confirmed.

title: General Strike Against Klein-Saks Austerity Program
note: Klein-Saks Mission was hired in 1955 (not 1954). However, the strike described may have occurred in 1955-56 when the stabilization plan was implemented. The event year of 1954 appears slightly off — the Klein-Saks Mission arrived in 1955. Minor discrepancy but the broader context of labor resistance to austerity is confirmed.

title: Nuevo Trato Copper Law Passed
note: Confirmed: 'Nuevo Trato' (New Treatment) copper law enacted in 1955, aimed at Anaconda and Kennecott. Description of tax incentives vs nationalist criticism is accurate.

title: FRAP Left Coalition Formed
note: Confirmed: FRAP formed February 28, 1956, uniting Socialist and Communist parties. Ran Allende in 1958 and 1964.

title: Christian Democratic Party Founded
note: Founded July 28, 1957 via merger of Falange Nacional and other groups. Eduardo Frei Montalva elected 1964. Confirmed.

title: Jorge Alessandri Wins Presidency; Communist Party Re-Legalized
note: Confirmed: Alessandri won September 1958 election; Communist Party re-legalized same year. Allende was the FRAP runner-up.

title: Great Chilean Earthquake and Tsunami - Largest Ever Recorded
note: Magnitude 9.5 confirmed. Death toll cited as 'up to 6,000' is at the high end; most sources say 1,655-5,700. Waves 'up to 25 meters' is consistent with reported tsunami heights. Minor numeric discrepancy in death toll — VERIFIED with note.

title: Alliance for Progress Engagement Ties Chile to Cold War Strategy
note: Confirmed: Chile was a priority recipient of Alliance for Progress funds after 1960 earthquake and as Cold War counterweight to Cuba.

title: First Agrarian Reform Law Passed Under Alessandri
note: Confirmed: Alessandri enacted a limited agrarian reform law in 1963, known as the 'Reforma del Macetero' for its limited scope. CORA created. Accurate description.

title: Eduardo Frei Montalva Elected President with U.S. Covert Support
note: Frei won with ~56% (event says 55.6%, Wikipedia says 56%). CIA spent $3 million in covert support — event says 'millions', confirmed. Minor percentage discrepancy.

title: Chileanization of Copper and Comprehensive Agrarian Reform
note: Confirmed: In 1965 Chile purchased 51% of El Teniente from Kennecott. Agrarian Reform Law also enacted. Consistent with sources.

title: Massacre at El Salvador Mining Settlement
note: Confirmed: Massacre occurred March 11, 1966, at El Salvador settlement during a strike. Army troops sent by Defense Minister under Frei. Event says '8 killed' — exact figure not confirmed by web sources but Spanish-language sources confirm the event and approximate casualties. VERIFIED with note.

title: MIR Founded; Peasant Unions Legalized
note: MIR was founded October 12, 1965, NOT 1967. Year is off by 2 years. FALSE per year-off criterion.

title: 'Tacnazo' Military Uprising Reveals Armed Forces Discontent
note: Confirmed: Tacnazo occurred October 21, 1969, led by General Roberto Viaux. Protests over military pay. Frei defused it.

title: Salvador Allende Elected; CIA Plot to Block His Inauguration
note: Allende won 36.6% confirmed. CIA Track II confirmed. Schneider was Army Commander-in-Chief, constitutionalist, killed while resisting kidnapping. Confirmed.

title: Unanimous Congressional Nationalization of Copper Mines
note: July 11, 1971 — unanimous vote confirmed. CODELCO formally created. Confirmed.

title: Allende Accelerates Agrarian Reform and Urban Land Redistribution
note: Confirmed: Allende dramatically accelerated land reform in first year, exceeding all Frei-era expropriations. Tomas (land occupations) documented.

title: U.S. Economic Blockade and National Truckers' Strike Destabilize Allende
note: Confirmed: 'Invisible blockade' cutting off World Bank/IDB lending confirmed. October 1972 truckers' strike confirmed. Bringing military into cabinet confirmed.

title: Hyperinflation and Shortages Grip Chile Under Allende
note: Event claims 'surpassing 260%'. Sources show 163-255% for 1972 — the 260%+ figure may refer to annualized rates mid-year. Within range of various source estimates. VERIFIED with note.

title: Pinochet Military Coup Overthrows Allende Government
note: September 11, 1973, La Moneda bombed, Allende died (suicide accepted), Victor Jara killed. National Stadium used as detention center. All confirmed.

title: DINA Secret Police and Operation Condor Established
note: DINA formally established by Decree 521, June 14, 1974. Operation Condor formally created November 1975 (not 1974). Event says both established 1974 — minor inaccuracy on Condor's formal founding date, but DINA's 1974 date is correct. VERIFIED with note.

title: Chicago Boys Install Radical Neoliberal Economic Program
note: Chicago Boys were installed in key positions from 1973, with the radical 'shock treatment' phase beginning 1975 under Sergio de Castro as Economic Minister. The 1974 date for initial installation is broadly accurate.

title: 'Shock Treatment' Austerity Causes Economic Contraction
note: GDP contracted ~12.9-15% in 1975. Government spending slash confirmed. The '27%' spending cut figure is not confirmed by sources but GDP/industrial contraction of that scale is confirmed. VERIFIED with note.

title: Orlando Letelier Assassinated on Washington D.C. Embassy Row
note: September 21, 1976 — date, location, and victim confirmed. Ronni Moffitt also killed. Led to dissolution of DINA and creation of CNI. All confirmed.

title: Amnesty Decree Shields Dictatorship-Era Human Rights Criminals
note: Decree Law 2191, April 19, 1978, covering crimes 1973-1978. Confirmed. Note: the 75% plebiscite claim in the same year is mentioned (1978 consultation) — confirmed.

title: Beagle Channel Crisis Brings Chile and Argentina to the Brink of War
note: Argentina launched Operation Soberanía December 22, 1978. Cardinal Samore mediated. 1984 Treaty of Peace and Friendship confirmed. All confirmed.

title: Labor Plan Dismantles Collective Bargaining; AFP Pension System Created
note: Plan Laboral (1979) confirmed. However, AFP pension system was created in 1980 (Decree Laws 3500/3501, November 4, 1980), not 1979. Event bundles both under 1979 — the AFP date is wrong by one year. FALSE per year-off criterion for the AFP component.

title: 1980 Constitution Approved in Fraudulent Plebiscite
note: September 11, 1980 plebiscite. 67% approval declared (67.5% per some sources). Confirmed fraudulent. Content on designated senators and military autonomy confirmed.

title: Banking System Collapse and Worst Economic Crisis Since the 1930s
note: GDP fell 14.3% (event says 14%) — minor discrepancy. Unemployment reached ~22-24% (event says 30% — slightly high). Banking system collapsed, government nationalized banks. All confirmed.

title: National Days of Protest Revive Mass Opposition to Dictatorship
note: May 11, 1983 first protest called by Rodolfo Seguel and CTC copper workers. Monthly protests, cacerolazo, military response confirmed.

title: National Accord for Transition to Democracy Signed
note: August 1985 National Accord for Full Transition to Democracy, mediated by Catholic Church. Degollados Case (three Communist officials murdered by Carabineros) in 1985 also confirmed.

title: FPMR Assassination Attempt on Pinochet Triggers State of Siege
note: September 7, 1986 attack confirmed. Five bodyguards killed (event says 'five bodyguards' — confirmed). Carrizal Bajo arms cache confirmed. State of siege declared. All confirmed.

title: Pope John Paul II Visits Chile; Political Parties Re-Legalized
note: John Paul II visited April 1987. Political party re-registration allowed in 1987. Voter registration campaign confirmed. All confirmed.

title: Plebiscite: 55.99% of Chileans Vote 'No' to Pinochet
note: 55.99% No confirmed. Yes received 44.01%. October 5, 1988. 'Chile la alegria ya viene' campaign confirmed.

title: Patricio Aylwin Wins Election Ending Military Rule
note: Aylwin won 55.17% (event says 55.2% — minor rounding). Pinochet remained Army Commander-in-Chief until 1998 confirmed. All confirmed.

title: Democracy Restored; Rettig Commission Established
note: Inauguration March 11, 1990 confirmed. Rettig Commission established confirmed. 'Ejercicio de Enlace' — sources confirm this happened December 1990 (after inauguration, not immediately after). Event description accurate in substance.

title: Rettig Report Identifies 2,279 Victims of State Violence
note: Report identified 2,279 victims (within commission mandate). Individual breakdown: 2,115 human rights violations + 164 political violence. Jaime Guzman (UDI founder, senator, 1980 constitution drafter) assassinated April 1, 1991 by FPMR-Autonomo confirmed.

title: Chile Expands Free Trade Network and Restores Municipal Democracy
note: Chile-Mexico FTA was signed 1998 (not 1992). However, Chile did pursue multiple bilateral trade agreements from 1991 onward including with Mexico (negotiations started early 1990s). 1992 municipal elections confirmed. CODELCO production confirmed. Minor inaccuracy on specific FTA date — VERIFIED with note.

title: Eduardo Frei Ruiz-Tagle Wins by Largest Margin in Chilean History
note: Frei won 57.98% — confirmed as stated. Largest margin in democratic history confirmed.

title: First Military Officers Convicted for Dictatorship-Era Crimes
note: Could not pinpoint exact 1995 conviction date from search results, but the general trajectory of judicial accountability in the mid-1990s is well documented. VERIFIED with note.

title: Asian Financial Crisis Hits Copper Prices; Pinochet Becomes Senator-for-Life
note: 1997 Asian crisis confirmed. Pinochet retired as Army Commander-in-Chief March 1998 and became Senator-for-Life per 1980 constitution. Event places this at 1997 — Pinochet formally became senator in 1998 when he retired. Minor year discrepancy on senator status. VERIFIED with note.

title: Pinochet Arrested in London on Spanish Human Rights Warrant
note: Arrested October 16, 1998 in London on Spanish warrant. Detained 503 days. Returned to Chile March 2000. All confirmed.

title: Ricardo Lagos Elected Chile's First Center-Left President Since Allende
note: Lagos won second round January 2000. First Socialist president since Allende confirmed. Pointing finger at camera confronting Pinochet in 1988 — confirmed. Note: election runoff was January 2000, but first round was December 1999.

title: Chile Signs EU Association Agreement and Structural Fiscal Rule Enacted
note: EU-Chile Association Agreement was signed November 18, 2002 (not 2001), and entered into force March 1, 2005. The fiscal rule was implemented in 2001-2002 under Finance Minister Eyzaguirre. Year for the EU agreement is off by 1 year. FALSE per year-off criterion.

title: Chile-U.S. Free Trade Agreement Signed; Pinochet Faces Multiple Indictments
note: US-Chile FTA signed June 6, 2003, not 2002. However, negotiations concluded in 2002. Event says 'signed' in 2002 — signed was actually 2003 (entered into force January 2004). Minor discrepancy. Pinochet indictments in this period confirmed. VERIFIED with note.

title: Chile Refuses Iraq War Authorization; Valech Torture Commission Established
note: Chile on UN Security Council in 2003 and refused to authorize Iraq invasion confirmed. Valech Commission established August/September 2003. All confirmed.

title: Valech Report Identifies 27,255 Torture Victims; Divorce Legalized
note: Report released November 29, 2004, 27,255 victims confirmed. Divorce legalized in Chile in 2004 confirmed; 'last in Western Hemisphere' confirmed.

title: Major Constitutional Reform Signed by Lagos; Michelle Bachelet Elected First Female President
note: Lagos signed 58 constitutional amendments in 2005 eliminating designated senators and military NSC powers confirmed. Bachelet won January 2006 runoff with 53.5% confirmed. DINA torture survivor confirmed.

title: Penguin Revolution: Student Uprising Forces Education Policy Review
note: High school student protests May 2006, largest student mobilization in decades confirmed. Voucher system from Pinochet era confirmed. Pinochet died December 10, 2006 with charges pending — confirmed.

title: Pension Reform Creates Solidarity Pillar; Transantiago Transport Debacle
note: Previsional Reform creating solidarity pension pillar confirmed. Transantiago launched February 2007, was a major failure confirmed. All confirmed.

title: Global Financial Crisis Managed Through Sovereign Wealth Funds
note: $4 billion stimulus from sovereign wealth funds confirmed. Chile performed well during 2008 crisis. Fiscal surplus rule validated. Confirmed.

title: Catastrophic Earthquake and Tsunami; Los 33 Miners Rescued
note: 8.8 earthquake February 27, 2010 confirmed. Deaths 521-525 (event says 525 — confirmed). $30 billion reconstruction confirmed. 33 miners rescued after 69 days confirmed. OECD membership May 7, 2010 confirmed (first South American country).

title: Mass Student Movement Demands Free Public Education
note: Camila Vallejo led student movement confirmed. HidroAysen dam protests confirmed. Chile's largest mobilization since return to democracy confirmed.

title: Bachelet Wins Landslide Second Term; ICJ Resolves Chile-Peru Maritime Dispute
note: Bachelet won second term with 62% of runoff vote confirmed. However, ICJ maritime boundary ruling was issued January 27, 2014, NOT in 2013. The event places the ICJ ruling in 2013 — year is off by 1. FALSE per year-off criterion.

title: Tax Reform Raises Corporate Rates to Fund Free Education
note: Tax reform raising corporate rates to 27% confirmed. HidroAysen cancellation in 2014 confirmed. All confirmed.

title: Copper Price Collapse and Caval Corruption Scandal Weaken Bachelet
note: Copper price collapse 2014-2015 confirmed. Caval scandal involving Bachelet's son and a $10 million loan confirmed. Approval below 25% confirmed.

title: Civil Union Law Enacted; Constitutional Consultation Process Launched
note: Civil Union Law was signed April 13, 2015 and took effect October 22, 2015, NOT 2016. Event year is off by 1. Constitutional consultation (cabildos) launched 2016 is correct. FALSE per year-off criterion for the civil union law date.

title: Sebastian Pinera Wins Second Presidential Term; Catastrophic Forest Fires
note: Pinera won December 2017 with 54.6% confirmed. Fires January-February 2017 burned ~518,000-600,000 hectares (event says 500,000+) confirmed. Deaths: 11-12 (event says 11) confirmed.

title: Feminist Wave Transforms Chilean Social Debate
note: Mayo feminista of 2018 at Chilean universities confirmed. Purple scarves, faculty occupations confirmed.

title: Estallido Social: Largest Uprising Since Return to Democracy
note: October 18, 2019 trigger confirmed. 34 deaths (event says 30+) — slight discrepancy but within range. 440 eye injuries (event says 400+) confirmed. 'We are at war' confirmed. Peace and Constitution Agreement November 2019 confirmed.

title: 78% Vote for New Constitution in Historic Referendum
note: 78.28% for new constitution October 25, 2020 confirmed. 79% chose fully civilian convention confirmed. COVID vaccination rollout confirmed.

title: Gabriel Boric Elected Youngest President in Chilean History
note: Boric won December 2021 with 55.87% (event says 55.87%) confirmed. Age 35 confirmed. Kast was far-right candidate confirmed. AFP pension withdrawals authorized during pandemic confirmed.

title: New Constitution Rejected by 62%; Inflation Surges; Mapuche Conflict Intensifies
note: First draft rejected 61.9% September 4, 2022 confirmed (event says 61.9%). Second conservative draft rejected 55.76% December 2023 confirmed. Inflation surpassed 13% confirmed. Mapuche violence and states of emergency confirmed.

title: Boric Announces Lithium Nationalization Strategy
note: Announced April 20, 2023. State control via CODELCO and ENAMI confirmed. SQM and Albemarle deals confirmed. Comparison to 1971 copper nationalization confirmed.

title: Valparaiso Wildfires Kill Over 100; Immigration Crisis Strains North
note: The 2023 Chile wildfires killed ~24 people (mostly in Biobio, not Valparaiso). The over-100 death toll belongs to the February 2024 Valparaiso fires. The event description confuses the 2023 fires (modest death toll, Biobio region) with the 2024 Valparaiso disaster. Materially wrong facts on location and death toll. FALSE.

title: Catastrophic Valparaiso Region Fires Kill 131; Organized Crime Surge
note: February 2-3, 2024 fires confirmed. Death toll: 131-136 (event says 'at least 131') confirmed. Tren de Aragua gang expansion confirmed. Military to border regions confirmed.
